patch_description: The current program uses a single fixed-scale zero-phase SG polish, which forces one smoothing strength everywhere: it either over-smooths quiet regions (hurting lag/responsiveness) or under-smooths volatile ones (hurting smoothness and false reversals). The best prior generation (0.65, slope_changes 65.8, false_reversals 44.4) used a volatility-blended multi-scale SG polish, and the current program already computes a local volatility proxy (r_arr) and keeps the stable fixed-Q Kalman + solve-based RTS smoother. This edit replaces the single-scale SG in Stage 2 with the multi-scale volatility-blended variant (soft Gaussian membership in volatility space centered at the 20/50/80 percentiles, three kernel scales), while keeping the confidence-gated trend lead of Stage 3 intact. This targets the weakest metrics — smoothness (0.23) and reversals (45.4) — by widening the effective kernel only where local volatility genuinely demands it, without adding lag in quiet regions. Q remains strictly fixed at 0.05·q_scale² and the RTS gain stays solve-based, per confirmed prior findings; no Q-scheduling, no 3-state model.
